subject: Draft redlines: flex-burst credits and throughput anchor for Dedicated pools
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: julia.torres@verdane.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Draft redlines: flex-burst credits and throughput anchor for Dedicated pools

Julia — attaching our suggested redlines and a short summary below. Thanks again for the detailed usage export — that made the math straightforward.

Attachment: Verdane-Redwood-TS-Comments.pdf (6 pages)

Summary of what we changed in the draft: 
- Flex-burst credits: introduced a capped burst pool ("flex-burst") that can be consumed above the committed baseline up to 20% of monthly vram-hours; unused credits do not roll over. This gives Verdane headroom for short spikes while preserving predictable commit economics.
- Throughput anchor: replaced the ambiguous "throughput guarantee" language with a clear definition: 99th percentile per-request latency for the declared model/seq-length at the committed throughput (measured in tokens/sec). Remedies are triggered only when both capacity and routing were available but missed the anchor for two consecutive production windows.
- Service credit ladder: moved to a graded credit matrix (0.5% / 2% / 5%) by outage class and number of missed windows rather than a flat percentage. Keeps incentives aligned while limiting outsized credits for transient infra events.

Key negotiation asks for Verdane to consider: 
1) Accept flex-burst up to 20% of committed vram-hours/month at a discounted overage rate vs. on-demand.
2) Allow one non-consecutive month of burst usage per quarter with partial rollover of up to 5% (optional add-on).
3) Narrow the remedy trigger so remediation applies after two production windows of miss, not immediately on a single spike.

Please let us know which items you want us to remove from the doc or where you need alternative wording. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Julia Torres <julia.torres@verdane.ai>

Cc: partners@verdane.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 14:07:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: flex-burst credits and throughput anchor for Dedicated pools

Thanks Mina — received and reviewed briefly with infra and procurement. A few quick reactions before we schedule a legal review: 

1) Flex-burst concept is attractive. Verdane asks that the overage pricing be a fixed uplift (e.g., committed rate + 35%) rather than a separate on-demand SKU — simplifies billing.
2) We need clarity on how vram-hours map to our multi-model routing (we run a mix of encoder/decoder variants). Is burst measured per pool or per model? Prefer per-pool, but need to ensure fairness.
3) The proposed remedy ladder looks reasonable; procurement wants a cap on annual service credits (e.g., max 10% of annual committed fees).

Next steps: legal will add redlines to the Word draft. Can you provide a short paragraph we can insert under 'Measurement' that defines vram-hour accounting for pooled multi-model setups? Also please include the proposed billing math for the 20% flex-burst example with Verdane's Q1 usage numbers (we attached usage_history for 2027-Q1).

We'll aim to return an annotated draft by Thu EOD. If possible, a 30-min sync Wed morning (CEST) would help.

Best,
Julia
Julia Torres
Procurement Manager — Verdane Systems
julia.torres@verdane.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: julia.torres@verdane.ai, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: flex-burst credits and throughput anchor for Dedicated pools

Julia / team — following up with the requested measurement paragraph and the billing worked example. Pasting below for quick insertion; full doc attached as 'proposed-sla-clause-v2.docx'.

Measurement paragraph (ready-to-copy):
"vram-hour accounting and pooling: Committed capacity is expressed in vram-hours per month and is provisioned at the pool level. For customers deploying multiple model variants on the same Dedicated pool, all model consumption contributes to the pool's aggregate vram-hour usage. For billing and burst calculations, we convert per-request GPU consumption to vram-hours using the runtime-observed per-token memory residency for each model variant at the declared sequence length. Burst consumption is measured at the pool level and debited against the customer's flex-burst allowance. Verdane's multi-model routing will not create independent per-model burst accounts unless explicitly requested and billed as separate pools."

Worked example (using Verdane Q1 data):
- Committed baseline: 120,000 vram-hours/month
- Flex-burst cap (20%): 24,000 vram-hours/month
- Committed rate: €0.42 per vram-hour (example)
- Flex-burst uplift: +35% => €0.567 per vram-hour
- If Verdane consumes 134,000 vram-hours in month X (14,000 over baseline), billing would charge: 120,000 * €0.42 + 14,000 * €0.567 = €50,400 + €7,938 = €58,338

Notes on measurement: we will expose token-level telemetry in the Console and provide a monthly reconciled usage export. We can also deliver a daily burn report during onboarding to tune pool sizing.

Happy to refine wording. If procurement wants a fixed uplift number we can bake that into the SOW.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

From: Julia Torres <julia.torres@verdane.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@verdane.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:44:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: flex-burst credits and throughput anchor for Dedicated pools

Karthik — this is helpful, thank you. A couple clarifying questions from our infra lead (copied on partners@) before legal redlines: 

- Does the conversion to vram-hours account for KV cache residency differences between encoder and decoder models? We have long-chat sessions where KV cache materially increases RAM residency.
- For the throughput anchor, does the 99th percentile measurement allow removal of outliers caused by customer-induced spikes (e.g., bulk import jobs)? We want to avoid Redwood being liable for spikes caused by our background jobs.

On the billing uplift: procurement prefers a fixed uplift as mentioned. Please confirm if Redwood can commit to a fixed uplift band for the first 12 months (e.g., +30–35% on the committed rate) in the SOW. That will be a gating item for our CFO.

We will push legal redlines Thu EOD as promised. Wed morning sync still works for me; propose 09:30 CEST.

—Julia

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: julia.torres@verdane.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: flex-burst credits and throughput anchor for Dedicated pools

Julia — quick responses to the two infra questions so your legal and infra teams can proceed: 

1) KV cache: yes, our conversion includes average KV-cache residency. The reconciled export contains a breakdown by model of (a) compute GPU time and (b) average GPU memory residency including KV state; both are used in the vram-hour calculation. We will add a short appendix to the SOW that defines how long-chat KV residency is measured (sample window + aggregation method).

2) Throughput anchor & outliers: we can include an explicit exclusion carve-out for customer-initiated heavy background jobs. Proposed wording: "Requests identified as non-production or bulk-import by the customer's route tags, or events creating >10x baseline per-minute traffic for >15 minutes and validated by both parties, will be excluded from 99th percentile SLA calculations for the purposes of remedy triggers." This requires Verdane to tag import routes or agree on an incident validation workflow.

3) Fixed uplift: we can commit to a fixed uplift of +33% on the committed rate for the first 12 months, after which uplift is revisited at renewal with 60 days' notice. We'll add that sentence to the SOW pricing table.

If those three points look good, I'll fold the exact clause language into the doc and send a redline version for your legal review (should hit your inbox Fri night CEST). Happy to confirm the Wed 09:30 CEST sync.

—Mina
